READ-ONLY research task. Do NOT create, edit, or comment on any Confluence or Jira content.

You are gathering everything DevOps-related from Confluence for the Zimmermann PWA Kit project (Salesforce PWA Kit / Managed Runtime, Contentful, SFCC). The output will be used to build a personal FED Lead workflow skill covering deploys, release cuts, tagging and releases.

Use the Atlassian MCP tools. Load them first with ToolSearch if they aren't available:
`select:mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_search,mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page,mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page_children,mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_comments,mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_search,mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue`

Search exhaustively. Suggested queries — run these AND follow whatever they lead to: `CI/CD`, `deployment`, `release`, `tagging`, `tag-based promotion`, `MRT`, `Managed Runtime`, `environment`, `env vars`, `promotion`, `hotfix`, `rollback`, `branching`, `GitFlow`, `release branch`, `deploy preview`, `BrowserStack`, `Zephyr`, `setup checklist`.

One page is known: the "7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist" is page ID `305430530`. Read it and its children and comments.

Report:

**1. THE DOCUMENTED PROCESS.** How is a release actually meant to happen, end to end — from a merged PR to production? Quote the steps verbatim. Name the page and page ID for every claim.

**2. ENVIRONMENTS.** Every environment named anywhere (dev, test, sit, staging/stg, uat, prod, preview) — what each is for, what deploys to it, who approves, and what the *exact* environment names are. There is a known trap where `stg` and `staging` are different strings and tooling keys off the real GitHub Environment name; look for anything like that.

**3. TAGGING AND PROMOTION.** Any documented tag scheme, promotion model, or proposal. There was a "tag-based promotion" proposal by the Lead Architect (Tim Lavelle) — find it, and find its current status: approved, in progress, superseded? Read the comments; decisions often live there.

**4. RELEASE BRANCHES.** Is there a documented release-branch model? Was one ever agreed? There was an open question about whether the PWA Kit repo needs a `release` branch for MRT — find how it was resolved.

**5. WHO OWNS WHAT.** Approvers, tier-1 groups, who can deploy to which environment, who cuts a release. Name roles and people where the docs do.

**6. OPEN ITEMS, GAPS AND CONTRADICTIONS.** Anything unresolved, anything where two pages disagree, anything marked TODO or pending a decision. Also: anything the docs claim that sounds like it may not be true — flag it as a claim to verify against the codebase rather than asserting it.

For every claim give the Confluence page title, page ID, and a verbatim quote. Distinguish what you VERIFIED by reading from what you inferred. If a search returns nothing, say so explicitly rather than inferring. End with a section headed exactly `What I could not verify`.

14. CI/CD & Environments
------------------------

This section probably belong to a DevOps TSD, but will put here temporarily until we have one.

### 14.1 Topology

A six-tier environment topology spans **Local → Dev → SIT → Stage → UAT → Prod**. Each tier (other than Local) has its own SFCC realm, Contentful environment, and MuleSoft connections. Ownership splits across three zones — Digital, IT/NewStore, and Shared (Digital + Business).

| # | Tier | Owner | Purpose | Third-party availability | Deploy trigger |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Local** | Digital | Feature build on developer machines | All services mocked (MSW stubs) | `npm start` |
| 2 | **Dev** | Digital | Integrated digital testing across all 6 storefronts, independent of NewStore | MuleSoft STG · NewStore Dev · Omneo STG · Narvar stub · Adyen sandbox | Merge to `develop` |
| 3 | **SIT** | IT / NewStore | NewStore SIT and regression on its own cadence | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Narvar STG · AP21 test | NewStore release cadence (parallel lane, non-blocking for Digital releases) |
| 4 | **Stage** (E2E) | Shared | End-to-end testing with all third parties live; time-boxed booked windows | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Omneo STG · Narvar STG · Adyen sandbox | Booked 2-week window |
| 5 | **UAT** | Shared | Business acceptance across all 6 regions | NewStore STG · Narvar STG · Omneo STG · Adyen sandbox | Business approval gate |
| 6 | **Prod** | Live | Production; AU canary then flag-flip to remaining regions | NewStore PROD · MuleSoft PROD · Omneo PROD · Narvar PROD · Adyen PROD | Release manager + canary gate |

Stage is the **contractual performance-test environment** referenced in §9.3 — it mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle class, CDN/edge configuration, SFCC realm tier).

### 14.2 Branch model

GitFlow with explicit back-merges to keep `develop` aligned with production.

| Branch | Branched from | Merges to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `feature/*` | `develop` | `develop` |
| `fix/*` | `develop` | `develop` |
| `release/*` | `develop` | `main` **and** `develop` |
| `fix/release-{version}-*` | the `release/*` branch | the `release/*` branch (forward-merged to `develop` via the release back-merge) |
| `hotfix/*` | `main` | `main` **and** `develop` |
| `develop`, `main` | — | protected; PR-only |

Release branches are supervised — code logic fixes go on a `fix/release-{version}-*` sub-branch rather than directly on the release branch. Releases and hotfixes always back-merge to `develop` so production fixes flow forward automatically.

### 14.3 CI workflows

**QA workflow (**`qa.yml`) — runs on every PR to `develop` and `release/**`. Code-correctness checks with no environment dependency:

* Unit tests (Vitest)
* Storybook interaction tests (`play` functions) and component-level accessibility checks via `@storybook/addon-a11y` (`storybook test --ci`)

**SIT gate (**`digital-sit.yml`) — runs on push/PR to `release/**`; on merge to `develop` it also deploys to the **Dev** environment (tier 2 in §14.1). Environment-dependent checks:

* Playwright `p0` priority specs
* Bundle-size check against the ceilings in §9
* Contract tests against the MuleSoft OpenAPI specification
* Lighthouse CI thresholds (Performance ≥ 0.80, Accessibility ≥ 0.90, Best Practices ≥ 0.90)
* Trend gate against the LHCI history server

### 14.4 Deployment

Deployment is via Salesforce Managed Runtime. Each tier maps to its own MRT target:

* **Dev** — deployed on merge to `develop`, gated on a clean SIT gate (§14.3)
* **SIT** — deployed on the NewStore release cadence, isolated from the Digital release path (failures do not block `release/**`)
* **Stage** — deployed on a booked 2-week window for full end-to-end testing with live third parties
* **UAT** — deployed for business acceptance; promotion requires Business sign-off
* **Prod** — release-manager-gated; AU canary first, then flag-flip to remaining regions

Production deploys are gated on a clean SIT gate run plus stakeholder approval through Stage and UAT.

MRT deployment targets map one-to-one to the topology: `dev | sit | stage | uat | production`.

## Scope of what I read

All in Confluence space **SFCC** ("Adobe SFCC"), `zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net`. Everything below is VERIFIED by reading the page unless explicitly marked inferred.

---

# 1. THE DOCUMENTED PROCESS

There is **no single end-to-end release runbook**. The process is spread across five pages that partly contradict each other. Here is the composite, with sources.

### 1a. Merged PR → develop → DEV/SIT (automated)

**PWA CI/CD Pipeline (GitHub Actions), ID `305561601`** — trigger matrix, verbatim:

> | Push to `develop` | `digital-sit.yml` | install → playwright-p0, lighthouse-ci, contract-tests, bundle-size → sit-gate → deploy-sit → tag-sit-deploy, tag-sprint |
> | PR targeting `release/**` | `digital-sit.yml` | install → playwright-p0, lighthouse-ci, contract-tests, bundle-size → sit-gate |
> | PR targeting `develop` or `release/**` | `qa.yml` | unit-tests, storybook-test (every PR, parallel) → e2e-browserstack (release/\*\* only) |

Job definitions on the same page:

> | `deploy-sit` | `digital-sit.yml` | Pushes and activates build on SIT MRT environment |
> | `tag-sit-deploy` | `digital-sit.yml` | Creates `sit/deploy/{date}-{sha}` git tag for NewStore traceability |
> | `tag-sprint` | `digital-sit.yml` | Creates `sprint/{N}/{date}` tag on sprint rollover |

### 1b. Cut a release branch

**Branching Guide (GitFlow), ID `304840733`**:

> Release branches are created by squad leads or CI from a tagged `develop` state — developers do not create these. They exist as deployment targets for the SIT gate and cross-browser tests.
> **Pattern:** `release/v0.1.0`, `release/digital/v1.0.0`.

Fixes on a release branch, verbatim:

> Do not edit the release branch directly for code changes. Branch off it instead so the CI gate runs against the fix before it lands.
> ```
> git checkout release/v0.1.0
> git pull origin release/v0.1.0
> git checkout -b fix/release-v0.1.0_short-description
> gh pr create --base release/v0.1.0 --title "fix(checkout): SFCC-999 payment error on SIT"
> ```
> **When direct commits to a release branch are acceptable:** only for changes with no logic — copy corrections, version number bumps, a boolean flag toggle. These require explicit squad lead approval before committing.

**Skills page, ID `297959425`** — pre-cut step:

> `/generate-changelog` … Builds a structured, four-audience changelog (dev team, QA, product, GitHub Release) from conventional commits and the upstream baseline. Writes to `docs/releases/`. **Use before cutting a release branch.**

### 1c. STAGE gate

**PWA CI/CD Pipeline, ID `305561601`**, verbatim:

> ### STAGE convergence gate
> STAGE promotion requires both the Digital SIT gate green and NewStore SIT to be complete. This is a **manual gate** enforced by the delivery team before raising a STAGE promotion PR, not an automated GitHub status check. Checklist before any STAGE PR:
> * [ ] `Digital SIT Gate` check is green on the release branch
> * [ ] NewStore team has confirmed SIT testing is complete for this sprint
> * [ ] Integration Lead and both squad leads have signed off

### 1d. Tag main after release merge

**Branching Guide, ID `304840733`**:

> Tags are created by running `scripts/tagRelease.sh v{version}` from `main` after the release PR is merged — this creates both `v{version}` and `release/digital/v{version}` tags.
> Sprint boundary tags (`sprint/{N}/{date}`) are created automatically by CI when `scripts/sprint.txt` is updated.

### 1e. Production

**Environment Topology & Promotion Path, ID `304840708`**:

> * Deploys from: release manager only — manual approval gate in GitHub Environments.
> * Canary: AU goes first; remaining regions open only after error rate < 0.5% over 2h on AU.
> * Rollback: `mrt:activate --target production --bundle-id <PREVIOUS_ID>`. 50-bundle retention (~30-day window).

**TSD – PWA, ID `256835585`, §14.4**:

> Production deploys are gated on a clean SIT gate run plus stakeholder approval through Stage and UAT.
> MRT deployment targets map one-to-one to the topology: `dev | sit | stage | uat | production`.

### 1f. Jira-side process

**Story Workflow, ID `247922696`**:

> | Testing | **In SIT** | QA | Change is deployed SIT environment and QA to validate the story… |
> | Testing | **Ready to deploy to UAT** | Developer | Developer that developed the story should deploy to UAT environment |
> | Ready for Release | **Ready for Release** | Dev Lead | Confirm UAT approval, release readiness, deployment steps, rollback plan, feature toggles, configuration changes, and release notes. Ensure the story is included in the correct release package. |

---

# 2. ENVIRONMENTS

## The stg / staging trap — CONFIRMED, and worse than described

**Proposed: Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow), ID `335216656`**, verbatim:

> **Use the actual GitHub Environment name, not the workflow-file suffix** — they diverge for `stg` (`deploy-stg.yml` targets the `staging` Environment, not `stg`; this exact mismatch already bit this repo once, see `deploy-stg.yml`'s fix history). Map each tier to its real Environment name explicitly, and fail closed on an unresolvable environment/API error — as opposed to a genuine first-ever deployment with no prior Deployment record at all, which should be allowed to proceed.

**Comment on Environment Topology & Promotion Path (ID `304840708`), comment ID `339836930`, author Tim Lavelle** — this is the load-bearing one:

> The **GitHub Environment secret scope** table on this page lists `staging`, `sit`, `pre-prod`, `uat`, `production`. The real GitHub Environments bound in `.github/workflows/deploy-*.yml` today are `dev`, `prod`, `sit`, `staging`, `test`, `uat` — confirmed directly from each workflow's `environment:` key. `pre-prod` and `production` don't exist as GitHub Environment names in this repo, and `dev`/`test` aren't in the table at all (`test` is a newer tier — `deploy-test.yml` — that likely postdates this page).
>
> There's a second, more load-bearing issue underneath the naming mismatch: this page's own Tier 2 (DEV) row labels its MRT target "MRT staging," and the secret-scope table lists `staging` as holding **Dev credentials, no reviewer required**. But `deploy-stg.yml` — the actual STAGE-tier deploy workflow — binds `environment: staging` in the repo today, not `deploy-dev.yml`. So the GitHub Environment literally named `staging` is gated to the STAGE tier's deploy, not DEV's, which is the opposite of what this table implies.

So: **`prod` is the real environment name, not `production`**, per that comment — even though `304840708` and TSD `256835585` both say `production`.
